Google’s labels change over time, so its current help pages are the place to check if a setting looks different. The class action Thele v. Google LLC (N.D. Cal.) alleges that on or around October 10, 2025, Google switched on its Gemini AI "smart features" by default across Gmail, Google Chat, and Google Meet, allowing the AI to access users' private communications without their consent. Plaintiffs say this amounts to unlawful wiretapping and eavesdropping under the California Invasion of Privacy Act and other privacy laws. These are unproven allegations; Google disputes them and says its smart features are optional and user-controlled. The lawsuit alleges Google's "smart features and personalization" settings let Gemini access Gmail, Chat, and Meet content by default. Google disputes that characterization and says these features are long-standing, optional, and controlled by the user. Whether the feature is active on your account depends on your settings. You can review and turn off "smart features and personalization" in Gmail's settings and in your Google Account's Data & privacy controls; exact labels can change over time. No. The case is at the complaint stage. There is no certified class, no settlement, and no claim form. The court dismissed the first amended complaint in July 2026, the plaintiffs filed a second amended complaint in August, and Google moved to dismiss that complaint on September 29, 2026. There is nothing to file at this time. In Gmail on the web, open Settings (the gear icon), choose "See all settings," and look for the "Smart features and personalization" controls, which you can switch off. You can also review related controls under your Google Account at Data & privacy. The exact wording and location of these settings can change, so check Google's current help pages if you cannot find them. The complaint seeks to represent a nationwide class of U.S. Google account holders whose private Gmail, Chat, and/or Meet communications were accessed by Gemini after smart features were enabled. The exact class definition and time period will be shaped as the case proceeds. No class has been certified.
